committees.name: Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee

dimensions.assessment: Affects infant formula manufacturers, infants consuming formula, and federal regulatory agencies.
dimensions.evidence: requires infant formula manufacturers to report to the FDA within one business day

dimensions.assessment: Imposes strict reporting and consultation mandates intended to improve product safety and supply chain stability.
dimensions.evidence: manufacturer shall... notify the Secretary of such result... promptly consult with the Secretary for proper isolation

dimensions.assessment: Requires ongoing federal reporting and agency engagement without explicitly stating new funding sums.
Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to alter manufacturer reporting timelines and mandate extensive multi-year agency reports.
dimensions.evidence: Section 412(e) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 350a(e)) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory changes combined with multi-year reporting requirements spanning five years.
dimensions.evidence: not less frequently than quarterly for the 5-year period thereafter

missing_information: Exact fiscal cost of implementing the reporting and review mandates
importance_detail.rationale: Imposes new one-business-day reporting requirements on infant formula manufacturers for microbial contamination and requires regular FDA reporting on supply chain safety.
